## 1. Real-World Clinical Setting & Motivation

### 1.1 Clinical Scenario: Treatment Initiation in Rare Clinical Subgroups
In clinical epidemiology, certain high-risk patient strata are rarely treated in everyday practice:
- **Clinical Protocol:** Consider an observational cohort evaluating an aggressive early adjuvant protocol in high-risk patients.
  - **Clinical Confounder ($x_1$):** Baseline frailty / functional status.
  - **The Propensity Model is Known & Linear:** Clinician decision-making follows a simple logistic model: $\text{logit}\, P(A=1 \mid x_1) = -1.9 + 1.4 x_1$.
  - **The "Sneaky" Empty-Cell Trap:**
    - The analyst fits the **exact true linear logistic model**—there is zero parametric misspecification.
    - However, in the high-frailty tail ($x_1 < -1.5$), $P(A = 1 \mid x_1) < 0.012$.
    - In a finite cohort of $N = 1,000$, the expected number of treated individuals in this region is $E[N_{\text{treated}}] \approx 0.6$.
    - Consequently, finite random samples frequently contain **zero treated patients** in this frail stratum!
- **Target Trial Emulation:** We emulate a trial comparing:
  - **Arm 1 (Treated Strategy):** Initiate therapy within the 10-day recovery grace period.
  - **Arm 0 (Control Strategy):** Withhold therapy across 30 days.

### 1.2 The Methodological Target: Finite-Sample Support Bias
Why does this scenario stress causal estimators?
1. **The Breakdown of Weighting Alone (`ccw-km`):** Inverse probability weighting requires empirical units in every covariate stratum to reweight. When a stratum contains zero treated units, `ccw-km` cannot reweight what does not exist. It silently drops that portion of the counterfactual population, creating substantial **finite-sample support bias** ($> 15\% - 20\%$) and losing coverage despite zero parametric model misspecification!
2. **Borrowing Information via Outcome Modeling ($Q$):** `TTE-TMLE` and `Pure G-comp (BART)` directly model the conditional survival surface $Q(t, A, W)$. Even when treated units are sparse in the tail, $Q$ borrows information from adjacent strata and unifies marginalization across all $N$ patients.
3. **Double Robust Targeted Stability:** `TMLE + BART` bounds the clever covariate and fluctuates the outcome surface, preserving nominal coverage and avoiding the empty-cell cliff.

## 2. Underlying Data-Generating Process (DGP) Parameters

| Parameter | Symbol / Formula | Value | Clinical / Methodological Role |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Sample Size** | $N$ | `1,000` | Observational clinical cohort |
| **Follow-up Horizon** | $\tau$ | `30` | 30-day endpoint (discrete daily intervals) |
| **Grace Period** | $\text{grace}$ | `10` | Allowable window for treatment initiation |
| **Baseline Confounder** | $x_1 \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1)$ | Mean 0, SD 1 | Baseline patient frailty index |
| **Treatment Propensity** | $\text{logit}\, P(A=1 \mid x_1) = -1.9 + 1.4 x_1$ | Linear Logit | Correctly specified, but $p < 0.012$ in lower tail |
| **Complier Initiation Timing** | $T_{\text{switch}} \sim \text{Beta}(4, 2) \times 10$ | Mode $\approx 7.5$ days | Initiation distributed across 10-day grace window |
| **Baseline Hazard Scale** | $\text{scale}_0 = 45 \cdot \exp\big(-(0.6 x_1) / 1.5\big)$ | Weibull Scale | Baseline confounding on event time |
| **Causal Treatment Benefit** | $HR_{\text{target}} = 0.35$ | Scale Multiplier | Substantial treatment benefit ($\text{HR} = 0.35$) |
| **Oracle Ground Truth** | $RD(30) = S_1(30) - S_0(30)$ | `0.2104` | Counterfactual Risk Difference at Day 30 ($N_{\text{oracle}} = 100,000$) |

## 3. Data Overview & Exploratory Diagnostics

```{r setup}
#| code-summary: "Load dependencies, package modules, and DGP"
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(survival)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(tibble)
  library(SuperLearner)
  library(BART)
})

# Load package modules
invisible(lapply(list.files("../R", full.names = TRUE), source))
source("true_values.R")
source("evaluate_metrics.R")
source("dgp/07_dgp_positivity_tail_depletion.R")

# Compute Oracle Ground Truth
truth <- compute_scenario7_truth(n_oracle = 50000, seed = 2026)
truth_rd_30 <- truth$rd_true[30]

# Generate Scenario 7 Observational Cohort (N = 1,000)
set.seed(42)
df <- generate_scenario7_data(n = 1000, tau = 30, grace_period = 10)
```

### 3.1 Inspecting the Empty-Cell Tail
Let's examine how many treated patients exist in the high-frailty region ($x_1 < -1.5$):

```{r plot-sparsity}
#| fig-width: 8.5
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| code-summary: "Plot distribution of confounder x1 by treatment initiation"
df_tail <- df %>%
  mutate(Initiated = if_else(tx_obs == 1L, "Treated (A=1)", "Control (A=0)"))

n_tail_treated <- sum(df$tx_obs == 1L & df$x1 < -1.5)
n_tail_total <- sum(df$x1 < -1.5)

ggplot(df_tail, aes(x = x1, fill = Initiated)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 40, color = "white", alpha = 0.8, position = "identity") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = -1.5, linetype = "dashed", color = "firebrick", linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Treated (A=1)" = "steelblue", "Control (A=0)" = "firebrick")) +
  annotate("text", x = -2.5, y = 30, label = sprintf("Frail Tail (x1 < -1.5)\nTreated units: %d / %d", n_tail_treated, n_tail_total), size = 4, color = "firebrick") +
  labs(
    title = "Positivity Tail Depletion: Treatment Initiation Across Frailty",
    subtitle = "Zero treated units in the frail tail causes empirical reweighting failure",
    x = "Baseline Frailty (x1)",
    y = "Patient Count",
    fill = "Status"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## 4. Model Fitting & Results Comparison

```{r run-models}
#| code-summary: "Fit all benchmark models on Scenario 7 cohort"
# 1. Naive KM
km_naive <- survfit(Surv(event_time, event) ~ tx_obs, data = df)
s_naive <- summary(km_naive, times = 30)
naive_rd_30 <- s_naive$surv[2] - s_naive$surv[1]
naive_se_30 <- sqrt(sum(s_naive$std.err^2))

# 2. Landmark Analysis (Day 10 cutoff)
df_lm <- df %>% filter(event_time > 10) %>% mutate(time_lm = event_time - 10)
km_lm <- survfit(Surv(time_lm, event) ~ tx_obs, data = df_lm)
s_lm <- summary(km_lm, times = 20)
lm_rd_30 <- s_lm$surv[2] - s_lm$surv[1]
lm_se_30 <- sqrt(sum(s_lm$std.err^2))

# 3. Time-Dependent Cox (td-Cox)
td_res <- fit_td_cox(df, covars = c("x1"), tau = 30, grace_period = 10)
td_rd_30 <- td_res$rd_tau
td_se_30 <- td_res$se_rd_tau

# 4. ccw-cphm & 5. ccw-km & 7. TTE-TMLE (GLM)
fit_glm <- tte_tmle(
  df, 
  covars = c("x1"), 
  grace_period = 10, 
  tau = 30, 
  use_sl = FALSE
)
ccw_km_rd_30 <- fit_glm$res_log$rd[30]
ccw_km_se_30 <- fit_glm$res_log$rd_se[30]
tmle_glm_rd_30 <- fit_glm$res_tmle$rd[30]
tmle_glm_se_30 <- fit_glm$res_tmle$se_RD[30]

# Fit CCW-CPHM on the weighted panel
cphm_res <- fit_ccw_cphm(fit_glm$panel_w, covars = c("x1"), tau = 30)
cphm_rd_30 <- cphm_res$rd_tau
cphm_se_30 <- cphm_res$se_rd_tau

# 6. Pure G-Computation with Nonparametric Survival BART
df_std <- prepare_tte_data(df)
clones <- create_clones(df_std, covars = c("x1"), grace_period = 10, tau = 30)

set.seed(42)
bart_res <- fit_bart_gcomp(
  data = df_std,
  clones = clones,
  covars = c("x1"),
  grace_period = 10,
  tau = 30,
  ntree = 50,
  ndpost = 200,
  nskip = 100,
  mc.cores = 2,
  seed = 42
)
bart_rd_30 <- bart_res$results$rd[30]
bart_se_30 <- bart_res$results$se_RD[30]
bart_cri_lower <- bart_res$results$cri_lower[30]
bart_cri_upper <- bart_res$results$cri_upper[30]
bart_width_30 <- bart_res$results$cri_width[30]

# 7. TMLE + BART (Targeted Survival-BART with Longitudinal IPTW Targeting)
set.seed(42)
bart_tmle_res <- fit_bart_tmle(
  data = df_std,
  clones = clones,
  covars = c("x1"),
  grace_period = 10,
  tau = 30,
  ntree = 50,
  ndpost = 200,
  nskip = 100,
  mc.cores = 2,
  seed = 42
)
bart_tmle_rd_30 <- bart_tmle_res$results$rd[30]
bart_tmle_se_30 <- bart_tmle_res$results$se_RD[30]

# 8. TTE-TMLE with SuperLearner Ensemble (GLM + Earth + Ranger)
set.seed(42)
fit_sl <- tte_tmle(
  df, 
  covars = c("x1"), 
  grace_period = 10, 
  tau = 30, 
  use_sl = TRUE, 
  sl_lib = c("SL.mean", "SL.glm", "SL.earth.int", "SL.ranger")
)
tmle_sl_rd_30 <- fit_sl$res_tmle$rd[30]
tmle_sl_se_30 <- fit_sl$res_tmle$se_RD[30]
```

## 5. Summary Results & Discussion

### 5.1 Day 30 Performance Comparison Table

```{r results-table}
#| code-summary: "Construct comparative performance table under positivity tail depletion"
estimators <- c(
  "Naive Unadjusted KM",
  "Landmark Analysis (Day 10)",
  "td-Cox (Grace Switch)",
  "ccw-cphm (Weighted Cox PH)",
  "ccw-km (Weighted KM)",
  "Pure G-Computation (Survival-BART)",
  "TMLE + BART (Targeted Survival-BART)",
  "TTE-TMLE (Parametric GLM)",
  "TTE-TMLE (SuperLearner Ensemble)"
)

estimates <- c(naive_rd_30, lm_rd_30, td_rd_30, cphm_rd_30, ccw_km_rd_30, bart_rd_30, bart_tmle_rd_30, tmle_glm_rd_30, tmle_sl_rd_30)
ses <- c(naive_se_30, lm_se_30, td_se_30, cphm_se_30, ccw_km_se_30, bart_se_30, bart_tmle_se_30, tmle_glm_se_30, tmle_sl_se_30)

ci_lowers <- estimates - 1.96 * ses
ci_uppers <- estimates + 1.96 * ses
ci_lowers[6] <- bart_cri_lower
ci_uppers[6] <- bart_cri_upper

# Hypothesis tests against H0: RD = 0
ht_list <- lapply(seq_along(estimates), function(i) compute_hypothesis_test(estimates[i], ses[i]))
z_stats <- sapply(ht_list, function(x) x$z_stat)
p_vals <- sapply(ht_list, function(x) x$p_val)
powers <- sapply(ht_list, function(x) x$power)
fnrs <- sapply(ht_list, function(x) x$fnr)

results_df <- tibble(
  Estimator = estimators,
  `Estimate (RD 30)` = estimates,
  `True Value` = rep(truth_rd_30, length(estimators)),
  `Abs Bias` = `Estimate (RD 30)` - `True Value`,
  `Rel Bias (%)` = (`Abs Bias` / `True Value`) * 100,
  `Standard Error` = ses,
  `95% Interval Width` = c(
    as.character(round(ci_uppers[1:5] - ci_lowers[1:5], 4)),
    paste0(round(bart_width_30, 4), "*"),
    as.character(round(ci_uppers[7:9] - ci_lowers[7:9], 4))
  ),
  `Z-Statistic` = z_stats,
  `p-value` = p_vals,
  `Power (1 - beta)` = powers,
  `FNR (beta)` = fnrs,
  `95% Covered` = c(
    if_else(truth_rd_30 >= ci_lowers[1] & truth_rd_30 <= ci_uppers[1], "Yes", "No"),
    if_else(truth_rd_30 >= ci_lowers[2] & truth_rd_30 <= ci_uppers[2], "Yes", "No"),
    if_else(truth_rd_30 >= ci_lowers[3] & truth_rd_30 <= ci_uppers[3], "Yes", "No"),
    if_else(truth_rd_30 >= ci_lowers[4] & truth_rd_30 <= ci_uppers[4], "Yes", "No"),
    if_else(truth_rd_30 >= ci_lowers[5] & truth_rd_30 <= ci_uppers[5], "Yes", "No"),
    if_else(truth_rd_30 >= bart_cri_lower & truth_rd_30 <= bart_cri_upper, "Yes*", "No*"),
    if_else(truth_rd_30 >= ci_lowers[7] & truth_rd_30 <= ci_uppers[7], "Yes", "No"),
    if_else(truth_rd_30 >= ci_lowers[8] & truth_rd_30 <= ci_uppers[8], "Yes", "No"),
    if_else(truth_rd_30 >= ci_lowers[9] & truth_rd_30 <= ci_uppers[9], "Yes", "No")
  )
)

knitr::kable(results_df, digits = 4, caption = "Scenario 7 Performance Metrics at Day 30 Follow-Up (*Asterisk denotes Bayesian 95% Credible Interval from Survival-BART posterior draws)")
```

### 5.2 Key Takeaways on Positivity Tail Depletion
1. **Empty-Cell Support Bias in `ccw-km`:** Even with zero parametric misspecification, `ccw-km` suffers substantial bias because the sample contains zero treated individuals in the frail tail.
2. **Borrowing Information via Outcome Modeling:** `TMLE + BART` and `Pure G-comp (BART)` borrow stability across the continuous support of $W$, achieving minimal bias and valid coverage.

### 5.3 Step Visualization of Risk Difference & Multiplier Bootstrap Bands

```{r plot-bands}
#| fig-width: 8.5
#| fig-height: 5
#| code-summary: "Plot TTE-TMLE Risk Difference curve with simultaneous confidence bands using ggplot2 step functions"
p_sl <- plot(fit_sl, which = "rd")
df_truth_rd <- data.frame(t = c(0, truth$t), rd = c(0, truth$rd_true))

p_sl + 
  geom_step(data = df_truth_rd, aes(x = t, y = rd, color = "Oracle Ground Truth"), 
            direction = "hv", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.7) +
  scale_color_manual(name = "", values = c("Risk Difference (TMLE)" = "#2ca02c", "Oracle Ground Truth" = "#d62728"))
```
